newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat futures end higher on Turkey rumblings.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat futures end higher on Turkey rumblings.

text.p: A technical bounce, rumors Turkey soon will be in the market for U.S. wheat and talk that USDA will cut the carryout tally for 1996-97 wheat stocks lifted CBOT soft red winter wheat to higher closes, traders said.
"It's all a technical recovery. The three wheats are feeding on each other," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures.
KCBT and MGE wheat futures also closed higher.
Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders Report showed as of November 5, speculators including funds, were short CBOT wheat by roughly two to one.
"Commission house and funds covered shorts and stops were hit from $3.81-1/2 to $3.83-1/2 (Dec)," Searcy said.

He and others said talk of Turkey was widespread but there was no confirmation Turkey was seeking wheat. Turkey's Grain Board last week said it may import 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes of wheat to curb rises in bread prices. Searcy said if a tender is held, it would be for U.S. wheat as the U.S. would be the only nation to grant credit for the Turkish purchases.
Wheat closed 1-3/4 to five cents per bushel higher, with December up 4-3/4 at $3.83-1/2.

USDA Tuesday at 0730 CST/1330 GMT will release its November crop production report and also reveal its updated supply/demand data. Some traders expect the supply/demand report to show a cut in the government's outlook for 1996-97 U.S. wheat ending stocks.

In October, USDA pegged the ending stocks for the 1996-97 marketing year which ends on May 31 to total 470 million bushels. The October report for wheat represented a cut in ending stocks from the 506 million bushels indicated on USDA's September report.
Wheat futures trading volume was thin with Continental Grain the key buyer of one million bushels of December, traders said.
Technicians cited wheat's near term oversold status as rationale for the gains.

But the nine day relative strength index (RSI) for the December was nearing neutral territory, closing at 46.5 points. The market considers an RSI of 30 or less as an oversold market and 70 or more as an overbought market.
The longer term moving averages remained bearish.
First resistance in the December was at $3.82 and second resistance was at $3.90. First support in the December was at $3.74 and second support was at $3.66.
The session high for December was $3.87.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 14,500 contracts, about the same as the 14,316 traded Friday.
In wheat options, Prudential Securities bought 250 December $3.70 puts at 1-3/4 cents and Rosenthal Collins bought 200 May $4.50 calls at 2-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 4,500 contracts, below the 5,124 traded Friday.
